title: GSI ledger check: CI refuses two new indexes on one table in one release, and warns near the table limit
description:
Outcome: There is no automated guard for the one-new-index-per-table-per-deploy rule today (only comments in scripts/test-reference-feed-keys.ts). Add a CI check that compares the indexes of every model with origin/develop's last release tag and fails when a table gains more than one index, when an index changes its keys in place, or when a table passes 18 indexes (DynamoDB's default limit is 20; Reference is at 15, 16 with PR #1239). It also prints the release order the upgrade planner (PPY-d2cab9) needs.

Touches (verified at origin/develop 23fabe1d): new scripts/test-gsi-ledger.ts, package.json test script, CI workflow, docs/releasing.md.

Acceptance (Gherkin feature file: features_backend/gsi-ledger.feature):
Scenario: Two new indexes on one table fail the build
    Given a change that adds two indexes to Reference
    When CI runs
    Then the GSI ledger check fails naming Reference and both indexes

Dependencies: blocked by nothing. Blocks PPY-1ce06f, PPY-297ebe. (Also recorded as kbs dependencies.)
Implements or extends: -.

Testing: Unit tests with schema fixtures.
Rollout: CI only; releasable immediately.
Risk and mitigation: Low. Risk: false failures on renamed indexes. Mitigation: a rename is reported as remove plus add, which is what DynamoDB does anyway.

Releasable on its own: yes.
DynamoDB index: none.
AppSync authorisation: unchanged.
Design note: docs/plans/multi-tenant-architecture.md (PR on branch docs/multi-tenant-architecture).
